title: The Clean Finish Is Punished
eyebrow: First of the gate fixes you asked for

actions.fyi: Nothing needed from you. You picked the gates to go first; this is the one that fires at the end of every tidy turn.

content.label: What goes wrong
content.lead: The gate that stops work happening off the books asks its question at the wrong moment.

rows.title: It counts every file changed since the turn began
Then it asks what the session is holding at the instant it stops
Closing your last ticket empties the second half while the first still holds the whole turn's work
rows.note: So the tidier the finish, the louder the accusation — and a session that claimed, landed and closed looks exactly like one that never claimed anything

content.label: Reproduced before anything was changed
content.lead: The gate driven directly with one made-up session, three cases, same three edited files each time.

rows: Held a ticket through every edit, closed it before stopping
Same edits, never claimed anything at all

blocks.label: The first and the third are the same to it
blocks.text: One of them is the correct end of a job and the other is work happening off the books. That is the whole fault: the gate cannot tell them apart, so it treats the good one as the bad one.

content.label: Fixed, and the teeth are still there
content.lead: Each change is now judged at the moment it was made. Same four cases, after.

rows: Held a ticket through every edit, closed it before stopping
Same edits, never claimed anything at all
Edits made after the ticket was already closed

blocks.label: Only the wrong refusal went away
blocks.text: A ticket claimed at any point in a turn covers that whole turn, which is exactly the leniency the old answer had — so nothing that used to be allowed is refused now. Everything that should be refused still is.

blocks.label: It cannot come back unnoticed, and that was shown rather than assumed
blocks.text: All four cases are in the board's own self-test, which needs no live board and leaves nothing behind. Run against the old code it fails by name — "a turn that held a card through every edit and closed it was refused" — and against the new code all four come out right. The check also has its own tripwire: if the gate ever stops running at all, the never-claimed case goes red instead, so it cannot come out green by doing nothing.

content.label: Checked on a real turn, not a made-up one
content.lead: The gate was run against this session's own record of the turn that built the fix.

rows.title: Ten changes made this turn, three tickets claimed and closed inside it
With the last ticket still open: the turn ends
With every ticket of the turn closed: the turn ends
rows.note: This is the exact thing that used to be refused, and it is the point of the whole fix

rows.title: Same ten changes with nothing ever claimed: still refused, naming the five files
rows.note: So the rule still has its teeth on real work, not only on an invented case

content.label: Found on the way, now owned

rows.title: The board's only self-test is never run by anything
rows.note: It has teeth and nobody pulls the lever. Putting it in the game's own check run is refused by your own earlier ruling, so it needs a runner of its own

rows.title: A job opened before the outside-reader rule existed lands unread, for life
rows.note: Each job stores the run of steps it was opened with, so an older one has no reading step and never gets one. This one is such a job

decisions.title: The gate is proved by making it refuse on purpose, before it is loosened
decisions.why: Every one of these gate tickets is a rule refusing correct work. Loosening one without first reproducing exactly what it refuses is how a gate ends up with no teeth at all.

decisions.title: The ticket's own definition of done names a file that was deleted, so it gets a new one
decisions.why: It asks for a case in a test file the manager had already ruled out of existence. The replacement is the board's surviving self-test, which needs no live board and leaves nothing behind.

decisions.title: One shortcut is kept on purpose, and written down
decisions.why: A ticket held with no claim on record — claimed before the board started keeping them, or on a line where its name was lost — covers the whole turn. That is exactly the old behaviour, kept so nothing that used to be allowed becomes refused, and it is the one way an unowned change can ride out under a ticket that arrived after it. It is on the board's debt list.

next.if_nothing: This one is on the main line and torn down. I move to the next gate: the one that gives a session two different names the moment it starts work.

steps.step: A session stops being refused its own ticket the moment it starts work
The queue everyone joins to land work stops refusing the step before it
